## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Atthassadvārajātaka* (Ja 84) is a short narrative from the Pali Jātaka collection. The Buddha delivered this discourse while residing at Jetavana concerning a seven-year-old boy in Sāvatthī, the son of a wealthy treasurer (*seṭṭhi*), who showed exceptional intelligence and an earnest desire for spiritual welfare (*atthakusala*) [Fausböll 1877]. The boy approached his father to inquire about the pathways leading to welfare and benefit (*atthassa dvārapañha*) [Fausböll 1877]. In response, the father—the Bodhisatta—explained the six gateways to great benefit in life, opening with the verse beginning *Ārogyam-icche paraman-ca lābham* ("Desire health as the ultimate gain") [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. Concluding the story (*samodhāna*), the Buddha revealed that the boy of the past was the boy of the present, while the treasurer was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1877].
